## Question and basis

Does the unchanged 1945 Antoine correlation reproduce the four published
heptane vapor pressures inside its stated range? This is **physical
validation**, comparing a model with independent observations. The accompanying
test protects the numerical comparison; agreement alone is not code verification.
The intended use is a reproducible teaching example, not equipment design.

Willingham et al. give VP-1 in equation (2), pp. 233–234, and its coefficients
in Table 3, p. 239, n-Heptane row:

\[
p/\mathrm{kPa}=0.1333224\,10^{6.90342-1268.636/(216.951+t/{}^\circ\mathrm C)},
\qquad t/{}^\circ\mathrm C=T/\mathrm K-273.15.
\]

The measurements are Busch et al., Table 2, heptane rows 2–5 (PDF p. 8,
letter H), in K and kPa. Row 1 is retained in the input but excluded because
298.2 K is below the model's 25.9 °C lower bound. No in-domain row is omitted
and no coefficient is adjusted. This is nominal pure heptane; the source's
supplier purity is ≥0.998 g g⁻¹ (Table 1). No composition conversion is made.

## Agreement found

{{< include results/summary.qmd >}}

{{< include results/comparison.qmd >}}

![Published heptane pressures (points) and unchanged VP-1 (line). Horizontal and vertical bars are the source's expanded measurement uncertainties, k=2; table rounding is additional. The line uses 151 retained model evaluations over the compared temperature interval.](figures/vapor-pressure.svg){#fig-vapor-pressure}

The model underpredicts every selected measurement. The residual magnitudes
remain below the 0.55 kPa teaching allowance derived in
[scientific context](../../docs/scientific/CONTEXT.md). The common negative sign may
reflect systematic measurement effects or correlation discrepancy; four
rounded observations cannot distinguish them. No fitting is used to remove it.
Pressure uncertainty and table rounding are comparable to the discrepancy, so
this comparison cannot establish sub-percent accuracy.

## Uncertainty and limits

Table 2 footnote a gives U(p)=0.3 kPa and
U(T)=0.115 K + 0.002|t/°C| K, both with coverage factor k=2. Rounding the
printed table adds up to 0.05 kPa and 0.05 K. The acceptance allowance adds
these contributions conservatively after bounding temperature sensitivity;
it is not a statistical confidence interval or a process-design specification.
The source provides no covariance for the 1945 coefficients. Historical
temperature-scale differences are not corrected, and no raw instrument record
is available in this example. The calculation is direct algebra; there is no
iterative solve or discretization to refine.

The four states support a limited physical comparison over 303.2–318.2 K.
They do not validate mixtures, extrapolation, critical-region behavior,
impurity effects, or general property-package accuracy. The modern paper also
compares its observations with NIST correlation values, so this reproduction
does not claim a new scientific finding.

## Reproducibility and sources

This notebook reads retained results only. `scripts/run.py` owns evaluation;
`scripts/present.py` reads `results/comparison.csv`, `results/model-curve.csv`,
and `results/summary.json` to prepare the single figure and includes above.
The table's extra calculated digits permit auditing and are not measurement
precision. See [input provenance](inputs/provenance.md) for original units,
row locators, download addresses, SHA-256 hashes, licence findings, and source
access notes. No source acquisition or numerical model runs during rendering.
